summary: Computes a viewport/window rectangle in pixels from normalized inputs. Reads a global screen scale pair (dword_8B8DD4 / dword_8B8DD8) or falls back to unity scale when a6 is set. Scales the normalized width/height/travel inputs by the scale factors when they are <= 1.0, converts to integer pixels via CRTFtol, writes width/height/center to integer fields (this+0x54/+0x58/+0x5C/+0x60/+0x64/+0x68) and float copies (this+0x14/+0x18), then derives projection terms: half-width this+0xC = 0.5*width/this+0x1C, half-height this+0x10 = 0.5*height/this+0x20, and aspect ratio this+0x74 = width/height. A flag bit at this+0x80 (0x10) controls whether the half-width term is negated.

local_names.a3: pixel conversion input for the center dimensions
local_names.a6: scale-mode selector; non-zero selects unity scale

operations.description: a6 selects the scale source: non-zero uses unity scale (v7=1.0, v18=1.0), zero reads the width/height scale globals dword_8B8DD4 and dword_8B8DD8
Normalized width a4 is multiplied by the width scale when a4 <= 1.0; normalized height a5 is multiplied by the height scale when a5 <= 1.0
Viewport width field this+0x54 is written with CRTFtol(width scale) when a4 >= 0.0, otherwise with literal 0
Viewport height field this+0x58 is written with CRTFtol(width scale) unless a5 < 0.0, in which case it is written with literal 0
Center input a3 is scaled by the height scale when a3 <= 1.0, then rounded twice via CRTFtol producing the integer center base
Write integer center X: this+0x5C = base + (width >> 1), and the float copy this+0x14 = same value; this+0x68 receives the first CRTFtol result
Write integer center Y: this+0x60 = (height >> 1) + second CRTFtol result, this+0x18 = float copy, this+0x64 receives the second CRTFtol result
Half-width projection: this+0xC = 0.5 * width / this+0x1C; half-height projection: this+0x10 = 0.5 * height / this+0x20
Aspect ratio this+0x74 = width / height computed from the two integer viewport dimensions
Flag test on byte this+0x80 bit 0x10: when bit 4 is clear, this+0xC is negated to -half-width
